title: What CPD does the EU Insurance Distribution Directive require?
description: What Article 10 of the Insurance Distribution Directive (EU) 2016/97 requires: 15 hours of CPD a year, knowledge areas, and records, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: The Insurance Distribution Directive, Directive (EU) 2016/97 (IDD), requires insurance and reinsurance intermediaries and the employees of insurers and intermediaries who carry out distribution to complete continuing professional training and development (CPD). Under Article 10(2), each home Member State must control and assess their knowledge and competence based on at least 15 hours of professional training or development per year, adjusted to the products sold, the type of distributor, and the role.
keyTakeaways: Article 10(2) of the IDD sets the EU floor: national mechanisms based on at least 15 hours of professional training or development per year for in-scope distributors and employees.
Hours must reflect the nature of the products sold, the type of distributor, the role, and the activity; Member States may require a certificate of successful completion.
Annex I lists minimum knowledge and competence areas for non-life insurance, insurance-based investment products, and life insurance.
Under Article 10(8), insurers must approve and regularly review internal policies for knowledge, CPD, and good repute, identify a responsible function, and keep up-to-date records.

The IDD is a directive, so the detailed rules come from national law; Portugal transposed it through Lei n.º 7/2019 of January 16, supervised by the Autoridade de Supervisão de Seguros e Fundos de Pensões (ASF).
regulator: National competent authorities for insurance distribution in each Member State (in Portugal, the Autoridade de Supervisão de Seguros e Fundos de Pensões, ASF), with the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA) at EU level
appliesTo: Insurance and reinsurance intermediaries, including brokers and agents, and their employees who carry out distribution
Employees of insurance and reinsurance undertakings who carry out insurance or reinsurance distribution
Persons within the management structure responsible for distribution, and all other persons directly involved in distribution
Ancillary insurance intermediaries, subject to requirements adjusted to their activity and products

sections.heading: What is the Insurance Distribution Directive and when did it apply?

blocks.text: The IDD is the EU's framework for selling and advising on insurance. [Directive (EU) 2016/97](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32016L0097) of January 20, 2016 recast the earlier Insurance Mediation Directive (2002/92/EC) and extended the rules to insurers selling directly. Its definition of insurance distribution covers advising on, proposing, and concluding insurance contracts, assisting in their administration and claims, and certain comparison website activity.

Directive (EU) 2018/411 moved the deadlines: under amended Article 42, Member States had to adopt national measures by July 1, 2018 and apply them from October 1, 2018 at the latest. This page states the position as at November 2026, based on the EUR-Lex [consolidated version of October 9, 2024](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02016L0097-20241009), the current consolidated text. The CPD wording in Article 10(2) is unchanged from the 2016 original.

blocks.title: Directive, not regulation
blocks.text: A directive binds Member States to a result and leaves the detailed rules to national law. The 15-hour figure is a floor that each Member State builds into its own CPD mechanism, and national rules can differ on how hours are counted, which activities qualify, and whether a certificate is needed.

sections.heading: What does Article 10 require for knowledge and CPD?

blocks.text: Article 10 has two training duties: appropriate knowledge and ability at entry (paragraph 1), and continuing professional training and development to keep it current (paragraph 2). The CPD sentence reads:

blocks.title: Directive (EU) 2016/97, Article 10(2)
blocks.text: "Home Member States shall ensure that insurance and reinsurance intermediaries and employees of insurance and reinsurance undertakings and employees of insurance and reinsurance intermediaries comply with continuing professional training and development requirements in order to maintain an adequate level of performance corresponding to the role they perform and the relevant market. To that end, home Member States shall have in place and publish mechanisms to control effectively and assess the knowledge and competence of insurance and reinsurance intermediaries and employees of insurance and reinsurance undertakings and employees of insurance and reinsurance intermediaries, based on at least 15 hours of professional training or development per year, taking into account the nature of the products sold, the type of distributor, the role they perform, and the activity carried out within the insurance or reinsurance distributor."

blocks.caption: Key elements of IDD Article 10 (as at November 2026)
head: Element
Provision
What it means for a training program
rows: Distributors and in-scope employees must have appropriate knowledge and ability before performing their duties
National mechanism based on at least 15 hours of professional training or development per year
Content and hours reflect products, distributor type, role, and activity; conditions adjusted for ancillary intermediaries
Member States may require successful completion to be proven by a certificate
Member States need not apply the rules to every person, but management responsible for distribution and everyone directly involved must demonstrate the necessary knowledge and ability
Intermediaries must demonstrate the Annex I knowledge and competence requirements
Insurers approve, implement, and regularly review policies; identify a responsible function; keep up-to-date records

blocks.text: Article 10(3) adds a good repute requirement, including a clean criminal record for serious offenses linked to crimes against property or other financial crimes, for natural persons directly involved in distribution.

sections.heading: What knowledge areas does Annex I list?

blocks.text: Annex I sets minimum professional knowledge and competence requirements by product type. It is the natural syllabus for both entry training and CPD planning.

items: **Non-life insurance (classes 1 to 18):** terms and conditions of policies, applicable distribution law such as consumer protection, tax, and social and labor law, claims handling, complaints handling, assessing customer needs, the insurance market, business ethics standards, and financial competency.

**Insurance-based investment products:** product terms and net premiums, guaranteed and non-guaranteed benefits, advantages and disadvantages of investment options, financial risks borne by policyholders, life and savings products, the pension system, applicable law, the insurance and savings markets, complaints, customer needs, conflicts of interest management, business ethics, and financial competency.

**Life insurance:** policy terms and guaranteed benefits, the national pension system, insurance contract law, consumer protection, data protection, anti-money laundering and, where applicable, tax and social and labor law, relevant markets, complaints, consumer needs, conflicts of interest, business ethics, and financial competency.

blocks.text: Because Annex I includes anti-money laundering and data protection for life business, CPD plans can link to related obligations, for example [Portugal's AML training duty](/regulations/portugal-aml-law-training-requirements) and [GDPR staff training](/regulations/gdpr-staff-training-requirements).

The 15-hour floor applies to intermediaries and to employees of insurers and intermediaries who carry out distribution, as defined in national law. Member States may exempt some natural persons in a distributor, but not the managers responsible for distribution or anyone directly involved in it.

For ancillary insurance intermediaries, such as businesses selling insurance as an add-on to goods or travel, Member States adjust the conditions to the particular activity and products. Member States may also require the undertaking or intermediary to verify the knowledge and ability of intermediaries it uses and, if needed, provide them with training corresponding to the products sold. Back-office staff with no distribution role are generally outside the hours requirement, but each national rule should be checked.

sections.heading: What happens if a distributor breaches Article 10?

blocks.text: Breaching Article 10 is a listed infringement under the IDD's sanctions article. Article 33(1)(d) covers "an insurance distributor who fails to meet the provisions of Article 10".

For that breach, Article 33(3) requires Member States to give competent authorities at least the power to order the person to cease and desist and, for an intermediary, to withdraw its registration. Article 33(4) allows Member States to add further sanctions and higher pecuniary penalties. The high minimum fines in Article 33(2), such as at least EUR 5,000,000 or up to 5% of annual turnover for legal persons, apply to breaches involving insurance-based investment products under point (e), not to Article 10 breaches as such.

sections.heading: How does Portugal apply the IDD?

blocks.text: Portugal transposed the IDD through Lei n.º 7/2019 of January 16, which approves the legal regime for insurance and reinsurance distribution, amends the insurance activity regime in Lei n.º 147/2015, and repeals Decreto-Lei n.º 144/2006. The [EUR-Lex national transposition record](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/NIM/?uri=CELEX:32016L0097) lists it among Portugal's measures, and its title names the Autoridade de Supervisão de Seguros e Fundos de Pensões (ASF) as the authority for related administrative offenses.

Portuguese distributors should take the exact CPD rules, including how hours are counted and evidenced, from Lei n.º 7/2019 as amended and from ASF regulations, which this page does not summarize. Groups operating in several Member States should plan one Annex I based curriculum with national supplements for hours, certification, and record formats.

sections.heading: How should an insurer plan and evidence 15 hours of CPD?

blocks.text: Plan CPD from the Annex I areas and the role, not from a catalog of courses, and record each activity against the area and the hours. The plan below is an illustrative example for a life and investment adviser; it is not an EU template, and national rules on qualifying activities apply.

blocks.caption: Illustrative CPD year for an adviser distributing life insurance and insurance-based investment products
head: Annex I area
Example activity
Hours
Evidence
rows: Products, terms, and guaranteed and non-guaranteed benefits
Training on two new product launches
Attendance record and product knowledge assessment
Applicable law: consumer protection, data protection, anti-money laundering
Annual regulatory update with scenario questions
Completion record with pass mark and content version
Assessing customer needs and conflicts of interest
Case review workshop on suitability and demands and needs
Workshop record and supervisor file review

blocks.text: The total of 15 hours meets the EU floor. Article 10(2) speaks of mechanisms to "control effectively and assess" knowledge and competence, so pair hours with assessment results, as described in [how to evidence training effectiveness to a regulator](/guides/how-to-evidence-training-effectiveness-to-a-regulator). A [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix) linking roles, Annex I areas, and hours makes the Article 10(8) records easier to produce.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models Annex I knowledge areas, products, and distribution roles as linked concepts with assessment points, so each CPD activity is tied to the area and role it serves. When a product or rule changes, the affected roles and content are identified from those links, and the record shows hours and assessed competence together. See [financial services](/industries/financial-services).

faqs.q: Is the IDD 15-hour CPD requirement per calendar year?
faqs.a: Article 10(2) says at least 15 hours of professional training or development per year. Whether the year is a calendar year, a rolling year, or a registration year, and how carry-over works, is set by each Member State's national rules, so check the home Member State's regulator.

faqs.q: Does e-learning count toward the 15 hours?
faqs.a: The IDD refers to professional training or development without naming formats, so it does not exclude e-learning. Member States decide which activities qualify and how they are evidenced, and some require proof by certificate. Pairing any format with an assessment supports the requirement to assess knowledge and competence.

faqs.q: Do insurance company back-office staff need 15 hours of CPD?
faqs.a: Not usually. Article 10(2) covers employees who carry out distribution, and Member States need not apply the rules to every person in an insurer. They must apply them to managers responsible for distribution and to everyone directly involved in distribution.

faqs.q: Who keeps CPD records under the IDD?
faqs.a: Article 10(8) requires insurance and reinsurance undertakings to establish, maintain, and keep up-to-date records of documentation on the application of the knowledge, CPD, and good repute requirements, and to identify a function responsible for implementing the related policies. National rules set the detail for intermediaries.

factCheck.claim: Article 10(2): CPD requirements for intermediaries and employees of undertakings and intermediaries; mechanisms based on at least 15 hours of professional training or development per year, taking into account products, distributor type, role and activity; Member States may require a certificate.

Consolidated version 09.10.2024 (amended by 2018/411, 2019/1935, 2023/2864, 2024/896) keeps the at least 15 hours wording; amended Article 42: adopt by 1 July 2018 and apply from 1 October 2018 at the latest.

Article 10(2) further subparagraphs: adjustment for ancillary intermediaries; undertakings may verify intermediaries' knowledge and provide training; management and persons directly involved must demonstrate knowledge; intermediaries demonstrate Annex I requirements. Annex I areas for non-life, IBIPs and life.
Article 10(8): undertakings approve, implement and regularly review internal policies, identify a function, keep up-to-date records for paragraphs 1 to 3. Article 10(3) good repute requirements.

Article 33(1)(d) covers a distributor failing to meet Article 10; Article 33(3) minimum powers for (a) to (d) and (f): cease and desist order, withdrawal of intermediary registration; Article 33(2) fines (EUR 5,000,000 or 5% turnover; EUR 700,000 natural persons) apply to point (e) IBIP breaches; Article 33(4) allows higher.
